item.title: Broken Ergodicity and the Violation of the Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem Lead to Generalization Beyond Overfitting in Machine Learning
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Chan Li, Nigel Goldenfeld
arXiv:2607.04135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The remarkable ability of modern neural networks to generalize improves with increasing network capacity, even when the number of model parameters or effective degrees of freedom exceeds the number of training data points. This phenomenon is all the more surprising given that generalization error diverges when the number of model parameters approaches a critical value from below. Here we use dynamical mean field theory to show that this so-called "double descent" behavior is the outcome of a phase transition in the stochastic field theory describing the training process. item.title: Quantum Destabilization of Skyrmions in Centrosymmetric Frustrated Magnets
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Amit Kumar, Kalpataru Pradhan
arXiv:2607.03378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the role of the spin quantum number s on the stability of skyrmions in a J₁₋J₂₋J₃ centrosymmetric quantum Heisenberg model on a square lattice using the neural network quantum states method. Our results reveal that the skyrmion stability Q is severely degraded when transitioning from the semiclassical regime to the extreme quantum limit (s=1/2), where it ultimately vanishes. We demonstrate that this destabilization is driven by quantum longitudinal fluctuations, with Q exhibiting a power-law decay as a function of the reciprocal spin moment 1/s. Spatial localization and prediction of deep concealed ore bodies is a major technical challenge in mineral resource exploration. Deep ore bodies exhibit strong spatial heterogeneity due to superimposed multi-stage geological processes. Sparse borehole data and high geological uncertainty further limit the applicability of conventional prediction methods. Existing approaches rely mainly on statistical interpolation and data-driven learning in Euclidean space. They struggle to capture spatial topological relationships among geological elements and cannot ensure geological plausibility under small-sample conditions.
